 Lesson 19 Battery Level Detection and
                          Alarm

19.1 Overview

In this lesson, we will learn how to detect the battery level of a power source connected to an
Adeept Robot HAT V3.2 using a Raspberry Pi. We'll also set up an alarm system that notifies us
when the battery level drops below a certain threshold.

19.2 Required Components

Components             Quantity  Picture

Raspberry Pi           1

Adeept Robot HAT V3.2  1

18650 Battery Holder   1

18650 Battery          2

19.3 Principle Introduction

Adeept Robot HAT V3.2 expands 8 ADC pins from I2C pins through the ADS7830 chip. The ADC

                                                                                                             support@adeept.com
     2
A1 pin is used for the Light Tracking interface, the A0 pin is used to detect battery power, and
the other 6 pins are on the board, as shown below:

The address occupied by the ADS7830 chip on Adeept Robot HAT V3.2 is 0x48
ADC is an electronic integrated circuit used to convert analog signals such as voltages to digital
or binary form consisting of 1s and 0s. The range of our ADC on Raspberry Pi is 8 bits, that
means the resolution is 2^8=256, and it represents a range will be divided equally to 256 parts.
The rage of analog values corresponds to ADC values. So the more bits the ADC has, the denser
the partition of analog will be and the greater the precision of the resulting conversion.

19.5 Demonstration

1. Remotely log:Remotely log in to the Raspberry Pi terminal.
2. Navigate to the Program Folder: Enter the following command in the terminal and press
Enter to access the folder where the program is located:
cd Adeept_PiCar-Pro/Examples/11_Voltage/

3. View Directory Contents: Type "ls" in the terminal and press Enter. This will display all the
files in the current directory, ensuring that the "BatteryLevelMonitoring.py" file is present:
ls

4.Run the Program: Enter the command below and press Enter to start the
BatteryLevelMonitoring.py program:
sudo python3 BatteryLevelMonitoring.py

5. Observation and Termination:After successfully running the program, you will see the
console continuously output the percentage of the current battery level. When the battery level
drops below 20%, a warning message will also be displayed., When you want to terminate a
running program, you can press the Ctrl+C shortcut key on the keyboard.

19.6 Code

Complete code refer to BatteryLevelMonitoring.py

           01 import time

                                                                                                             support@adeept.com
5

   02 import board

   03 import busio

   04 from adafruit_bus_device.i2c_device import I2CDevice

   05

   06 i2c = busio.I2C(board.SCL, board.SDA)

   07 # ADS7830 adress 0x48

   08 device = I2CDevice(i2c, 0x48)

   09

   10 # Define constants

   11 Vref = 8.4

   12 WarningThreshold = 6.75

   13 R15 = 3000

   14 R17 = 1000

   15 DivisionRatio = R17 / (R15 + R17)

   16

   17 #Define the ADC channel and command.

   18 cmd = 0x84

   19 channel = 0

   20 control_byte = cmd | (((channel << 2 | channel >> 1) & 0x07) << 4)

   21

   22 if __name__ == "__main__":

   23  buffer = [1]

   24  while True:

   25  device.write_then_readinto(bytes([control_byte]), buffer)

   26  adcValue = buffer[0]

   27  print(str(adcValue))

   28  A0Voltage = (adcValue / 255) * 5

   29  ActualBatteryVoltage = A0Voltage / DivisionRatio

   30

   31  BatteryPercentage = (ActualBatteryVoltage - WarningThreshold) / (Vref - WarningThreshold) * 100

   32

   33  print(f"Current battery level: {BatteryPercentage:.2f} %")

   34

   35  # Battery level warning judgment

   36  if BatteryPercentage < 20:

   37              print("Warning! The battery level is too low. Please charge in time!")

   38  time.sleep(0.5)

 Code explanation

First, initialize the I2C bus and the device, and define constants and communication control bytes.
In the main loop, send commands to the chip to read the ADC value. After conversion, calculate
the actual battery voltage and the battery percentage, and then output the results. If the battery
percentage is below 20%, a warning will be issued. The monitoring is performed every 0.5
seconds.
